name: Goutou (狗头) doge emoji
blurb: The doge face Chinese users add to a joke to say "I'm kidding, don't attack me"
title: Goutou (狗头) Doge Meme: Meaning, Origin & Use
description: Goutou (狗头) is the doge emoji Chinese users add to sarcasm; 狗头保命 means adding it so nobody takes a joke seriously. It comes from the 2013 Doge meme.
h1: What does 狗头 (goutou) mean in Chinese?
answer: 狗头 (goutou, "dog head") is the cartoon doge face, a smug Shiba Inu, that Chinese users put after a sarcastic or teasing comment. The phrase 狗头保命 ("dog head to save my life") means adding it so readers know you are joking and do not pile on you. The face comes from the Doge meme, based on a 2010 photo of the Shiba Inu Kabosu, which spread worldwide in 2013 and the same year reached Chinese social media, where Weibo made it a built-in emoji.

body: On Weibo, Bilibili, WeChat and most Chinese apps, typing [doge] or picking the dog sticker inserts a yellow Shiba face with a side-eye. Written text can easily read as hostile, so people add it to mark irony: the comment says one thing, the doge says "not really".
That is the core of 狗头保命: the dog head works like a shield. Commenters even call people out for forgetting it, with jokes like "no dog head, not on our side, get them!"

head: Date
Event
rows: Kabosu's owner, Atsuko Sato, posts the side-eye photo on her blog
The Doge meme spreads worldwide and reaches Chinese social media, where Weibo later makes it a built-in emoji
Weibo's ten-year statistics list [doge] as its fifth most-used emoji, used about 2.1 billion times
狗头保命 becomes a standard phrase for adding the doge face to sarcastic comments
Chinese internet companies apply to register trademarks for the cartoon dog-head emoji
Kabosu, the dog behind the face, dies at 18

ul: "Our boss is a genius, truly [doge]" (meaning the opposite)
"狗头保命" written out when no sticker is available
"Added the dog head, please don't attack me"
Variants in sticker packs: dog heads with sunglasses, helmets or tears

body: Goutou is still everywhere in Chinese comments and is one of the most important tone markers online, much like "/s" or "jk" in English. It is so common that a comment ending in [doge] is read as a joke by default.

faq.q: What does 狗头保命 mean?
faq.a: "Dog head to save my life": adding the doge emoji to a sarcastic or edgy comment so that others know it is a joke and do not attack you.

faq.q: Is 狗头 the same as the Doge meme?
faq.a: It comes from it. 狗头 is the cartoon version of the Doge Shiba Inu face used as a built-in emoji on Chinese platforms.
Roughly "/s", "jk" or a winking emoji: a signal that you do not mean it literally.
